blockingIssues.problem: The rationale states that the added hierarchy rule caused the shift toward orchestration in the candidate runs. The source documents a temporal association (the candidate prompt included the new rule and candidate outputs emphasized orchestration) but does not establish causation. The experiment report itself notes limitations that leave open other explanations (e.g., model-backend variability, no temperature/seed control) and frames the result as the candidate prompt being insufficient to preserve editorial intent rather than definitively attributing the shift to the new rule.
blockingIssues.sourceEvidence: The report records that "The candidate added one generic section, 'Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis.'" and that "Candidate outputs ... consistently subordinated company identity and audience scope while making orchestration the central positioning." It also lists limitations: "the model provider may change the backend behind an alias" and "No seed or temperature override was available," and concludes "the candidate prompt was not sufficient to protect the supplied editorial intent."
blockingIssues.constraint: The idea must not present the prompt change as the proven cause of the observed shift. It should describe the association observed in the experiment and preserve the source's attribution and limitations (i.e., report that candidate runs coincided with a shift toward orchestration and that the experiment concluded the candidate prompt failed to preserve intent, without asserting definitive causation).
